units: <cite ref="Bava Batra 56b:5">B. Bath. 56ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 19:15">Deut. XIX, 15</cite>) <he>ד׳ ולא חצי ד׳</he> a statement (testimony) but not a partial statement. Mekh. Bo, introd. <he>היה הד׳ לאהרן</he> (Tanḥ. ib. 5 <he>דבור</he>) the word of the Lord came to &c.; a. fr.—<he>דְּבַר תורה</he> according to the Biblical law.
<cite ref="Eruvin 81a:6">Erub. 81</cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>דְּבָרִים</he>, constr. <he>דִּבְרֵי</he>. <he>ד׳ תורה</he> Biblical laws; <he>ד׳ סופרים</he> Rabbinical laws.
<cite ref="Eruvin 81a:6">Ib.</cite>
<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 9:3">Yeb. IX, 3</cite>; a. fr.—<he>ד׳ קבלה</he> prophetic exhortations or incidental utterances in other Biblical books than the Pentateuch.
<cite ref="Chagigah 10b:10">Ḥag. 10ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Niddah 23a:6">Nidd. 23ᵃ</cite>; a. e.—

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 49a:6">B. Mets. 49ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bekhorot 13b:2">Bekh. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>ד׳ יש בהם משום מחוסרי אמנה</he> to word of mouth the rules concerning the faithless are applied, i.e. a verbal agreement is morally binding.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 48a:13">B. Mets. 48ᵃ</cite> <he>הנושא ונותן בד׳ וכ׳</he> he who contracts verbally has no legal claim.

Ib. ד׳ ואיכא … קאי באבל he who retracts a verbal transaction with which a payment of money was connected, comes under the category of those against whom the words ‘but the scholars declared’ (ib. IV, 2) has been pronounced.—דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים the Book of Chronicles.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 1:14">Lev. R. s. 1</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 14b:8">B. Bath. 14ᵇ</cite>.—<he>דָּבָר אַחֵר</he> (abbrev. <he>ד״א</he>) another interpretation (is this).
Gen. R. s. 1, beg.; a. fr.—2) thing, affair, object, occurrence &c.
<cite ref="Sotah 28b:4">Sot. 28ᵇ</cite> <he>ד׳ שיש בו דעת לישאל</he> an object which has sense to ask, i.e. a rational being, opp. <he>ד׳ שאין וכ׳</he> dumb creatures &c.—

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 11:7">Num. R. s. 11</cite> <he>ד׳ שבינך לבינו</he> that which concerns only thy relation to God; v. <cite ref="B00638"><he>בֵּין</he></cite>.—<he>ד׳ שבממון</he> a monetary affair.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 94a:5">B. Mets. 94ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—<he>ד׳ הלמד מענינו</he> a thing (law) derived from the context on the very subject. Sifra, introd.; a. fr.—<he>ד׳ אחר</he> (abbr. <he>ד״א</he>) something not to be named,
<cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 13:10">Men. XIII, 10</cite> <he>ואין צריך לומר לד״א</he> much less priests who have been offering to idols; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Shabbat 129a:7">Sabb. 129ᵃ</cite> sq.; a. e.—

Ib. 17ᵇ על בנותיהן משום ד״א ועל ד״א משום ד״א they forbade connection with their daughters on account of idolatry, and decreed something else (that a gentile child should be unclean as though afflicted with gonorrhœa) on account of sodomy.
units: Ber. 8ᵇ צנועין בד״א chaste in marital life; a. fr.—Pl. as above.—בעל ד׳ the person to deal with, opponent, party.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 14a:10">B. Mets. 14ᵃ</cite> <he>לאו ב״ד דידי את</he> I have nothing to do with thee; a. fr.—<he>לא היו ד׳ מעולם</he> there were no such things, I deny it outright.
